target_material: Nickel nitride (Ni3N) and nickel (Ni) thin films
summary: This study describes a low-temperature atomic layer deposition (ALD) process for nickel nitride (Ni3N) and nickel (Ni) thin films using NiCl2(TMPDA) as the metal precursor and tert-butylhydrazine (TBH) as the reducing agent. The films are grown at low temperatures (190–250 /C14 C) and exhibit low resistivity values. Postdeposition reduction at 150 /C14 C in 10% forming gas converts the nitride films to ferromagnetic Ni metal. The process allows for the deposition on both insulating and conductive substrates.
evidence: This article describes the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of nickel nitride and nickel thin films using a diamine adduct of Ni(II) chloride, NiCl2(TMPDA), as the metal precursor. Owing to the high reducing power of tert-butylhydrazine (TBH), the films are grown at low temperatures of 190 –250 /C14 C. The films are characterized in terms of crystallinity, morphology, composition, resistivity, and coercivity. X-ray diffraction shows reflections compatible with either hexagonal Ni or Ni3N. Composition analyses suggest that the films are close to stoichiometric Ni3N. Despite the nitride component, the films exhibit low resistivity values and at the lowest, a resistivity of 37 μΩ cm is achieved. The result is lower than what is typically observed for Ni xN films and not much higher than the best results concerning ALD Ni metal. The nitrogen content of the films is lowered down to 1.2 at% by postdeposition reduction at 150 /C14 C in 10% forming gas. After the reduction, the nonmagnetic nitride films are converted to ferromagnetic Ni metal.
